title: Implement sparse XOR batches on fixed physical tapes
body:
The physical Compact controller used uniform `rho+jK` positions. I add one borrowed encoded source/target-pair tape and implement a simultaneous sparse XOR batch after reservoir placement.

I use fixed fields `(u,t,y,b)`, with disjoint target guards and sources outside the target set, including sources inside guards. I execute twelve B1 interchanges and ten controlled rotations per complete row, then repair exceptional records with `T(S^-1(q))` using current inverse controls. I restore dirty fields and other address bits, preserve complete Gaussian records and borrowed input, and return a protected output with owned work erased.

I prove the source-relative bill

    12 K_q V(1+H^tau) + O(V + M A^6 + delta M A(R+A)),
    tau=332353/332929,
    delta=min(1,k(2/2^G+8*2^G/2^K)).

I include descriptor storage and repeated scans in A and price each interchange at the supplied H, including inactive high digits. Under the stated finite guard, source-admissible ordinary/refinement premises and actual long-record domain, I obtain `O(V(1+H^tau))` time and `O(V)+F_q` space. I bound scratch from the call structure, separately from observed peaks.

Validation at `c6020096322012f7cc41236c3ac15a6b6cd3f8b9`:

- I passed all six registered suites with CPython 3.12.13 and `-I -O -Werror -B`, plus metadata/pins and committed-byte/source-history checks.
- I checked 96 encoded states and 960 offsets, including unequal gaps, inactive high digits, whole-modulus wrap, prefix-only reads and current inverse controls.
- I checked a complete 256-record packet with 32 guarded and 224 exceptional addresses, two-row reuse, and a complete 2,048-record two-pair packet with cross-guard sources. I tracked each independent input bit and observed twelve B1 calls and ten rotations per row in both nonempty cases, with the retuned profile at each actual selector call.
- I reject malformed descriptors, omitted repair/inverse work, protected-output overwrite, borrowed aliasing, physical allocation, stale/altered source cohorts and the old ordinary profile. I also check the empty-list path with unused large guard parameters.
- I exported and checked 20 committed package/input files, replayed all six commands outside Git, and verified unchanged bytes for all 21 regular files including the receipt. Export SHA256: `c5767f3744338bb022a5d18863566da19c26a657be8b23b3a2ae775c431c7af5`.
- I passed [CI run39112383668](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39112383668) on the same head, including all six registered groups and the unchanged-committed-input check.

The multi-pair fixture has an entirely exceptional domain; I use it to test complete repair semantics. The physical fixtures use reduced fields and the elementary B1 branch. I do not execute the production GL64 program, prove the inherited all-size premises from tests, or infer sparse-density performance from that all-bad fixture.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/physical-sparse-xor-batch
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/physical-sparse-xor-batch --check-source-history
```

I started from main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6, and add one isolated package. The final refresh covered 321 open PRs and 2,440 Discussion records through 08:34 UTC on 2026-10-18. I found no competing encoded batch in that coverage. [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2612#discussioncomment-19009513).

I retain Vlado Vojdanovski's PR1673 unequal-gap algebra, Douglas Colkitt's compact construction, Jose Manuel's PR3055 physical Compact and PR3562 rate proof, and the David Arias/Nick Petalas/Adam Gall native and borrowing lineage in their source notices. I compare all 23 active ordinary files with the retained rate proof. Hiroki Kumazaki contributes concurrent retuned-factory work in PR3576. Nick Petalas's PR3581 restricts materialized B1-only exposure; I use the richer rotation/repair alphabet and charge its work.

I leave full reservoir placement, matching/color scheduling, combined PR3599/T74 integration, outer error/packing and independent scientific review open. I leave the selected frontier unchanged. Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
